Active Torque Control 4WD Outline
Active Torque Control 4WD has been adopted. By controlling the transmitted torque of the electronically controlled coupling located at the front of the rear differential, the front/rear torque distribution is continuously varied between the front-wheel drive state and direct-coupled 4WD, achieving optimum driving force distribution under various driving conditions for stability and low fuel consumption.
A differential limiting mechanism, as in a typical full-time 4WD, is not required, and the system has been simplified to reduce size and weight.
Features of Active Torque Control 4WD
Traction Performance Stable starting and acceleration on slippery roads such as snowy roads, equivalent to direct-coupled 4WD
Stability Stable cornering performance
Fuel Economy Low fuel consumption by distributing torque to the rear wheels only when needed and only as much as needed
The torque transmitted to the rear wheels is controlled by the Active Torque Control 4WD computer to achieve the optimum front/rear torque distribution based on input signals from various sensors.
Active Torque Control 4WD System Diagram
Main Components and Functions
Main Components Function
4WD Auto Mode Switch Switches between 4WD auto mode and FF (front-wheel drive) mode.
4WD Auto Mode Indicator Informs the driver of the 4WD auto mode control status by illuminating the light. When 4WD auto mode is ON, the light blinks 2 times and then illuminates, and when 4WD auto mode is OFF, the light goes off. In addition, if excessive driving during 4WD control may damage the drive system, the light blinks.
Master Warning Indicator Light Warns the driver of a 4WD system malfunction by illuminating the light.
Multi-information Display Informs the driver of a 4WD system malfunction by illuminating the master warning indicator light and displaying it on the multi-information display.
Semiconductor Type Wheel Speed Sensor & Rotor Detects the wheel speed of each of the 4 wheels and inputs it to the skid control computer.
Stop Light Switch Detects the brake operation state and inputs it to the skid control computer.
Parking Brake Switch Detects parking brake operation and inputs it to the main body ECU (instrument panel junction block assembly).
Shift Position Sensor Detects the shift position and inputs it to the engine control computer.
Throttle Position Sensor Inputs the throttle valve opening to the engine control computer.
Crankshaft Position Sensor Detects the engine speed and inputs it to the engine control computer.
Electronically Controlled Coupling Distributes transmitted torque to the rear wheels according to the output signal from the Active Torque Control 4WD computer.
Skid Control Computer Detects the signals from the semiconductor type wheel speed sensors, G sensor and stop light switch and outputs them to the Active Torque Control 4WD computer via CAN communication.
Engine Control Computer Detects the signals from the shift position sensor, throttle position sensor and crank position sensor and outputs them to the Active Torque Control 4WD computer via CAN communication.
Main Body ECU (Instrument Panel Junction Block Assembly) Detects the parking brake switch signal and outputs it to the Active Torque Control 4WD computer via CAN communication.
Active Torque Control 4WD Computer Detects the driving condition from the signals from each ECU, sensor and switch, and outputs a control signal to the electronically controlled coupling to distribute the optimum torque to the rear wheels according to the driving situation.
Signals and Functions
Signal Function
4WD Auto Mode Switch Signal Controls switching to 4WD auto mode or FF (front-wheel drive) mode according to the ON/OFF state of the 4WD auto mode switch.
Wheel Speed Signal Calculates the estimated vehicle body speed, front/rear differential rotation speed, etc. for use in each control.
Throttle Valve Opening Signal Calculates the torque output from the engine as driving torque.
Engine Speed Signal
Shift Position Signal
Longitudinal G Signal In starting control, estimates the uphill angle from the longitudinal G while stopped and applies pre-torque.
Brake Signal Performs control based on the brake signal to ensure braking and ABS performance.
Parking Brake Signal Control is basically stopped when the parking brake is applied.
